changes: Window run files and their manifest now use the shared optional atomic checkpoint batch boundary.
Sort and window share the same success, cancellation, version-conflict and write-failure test matrix.
Adapters without batch capability retain their existing behavior.

scenarios: Prior manifest remains readable and staged run remains invisible before commit.
Successful commit publishes both run and manifest with correct result rows.
Cancellation, conflict and final-write failure preserve prior or competing manifest without publishing the run.
Query reservations return to zero for every outcome.

limitations: These transaction tests use controlled scanner rows and MemorySpillAdapter, not a cloud spill service.
No multi-file atomicity guarantee for adapters without beginWriteBatch.
Cancellation after successful commit cannot retract published data.
Whole-Worker heap bounds and full audit acceptance remain open.
